paper.title: Neural network variational Monte Carlo for positronic chemistry

results.system_description: LiH at R = 2.815 bohr, all electrons, singlet (2 up, 2 down), clamped nuclei
results.variant: FermiNet (Spencer et al. architecture), bare molecule
results.source_location: Supplementary Data Tables, Lithium hydride, bond length 2.815 a0, 'Bare' column
results.eligibility_evidence: VMC energy of the bare molecule with the Spencer et al. FermiNet; 'Errors in energy expectation values are evaluated using a reblocking approach' (main text), printed in the sigma column.
results.notes: Printed as '-8.069021' with sigma_Bare = 0.000004 in a separate column. N_up = N_down = 2. The positronic energies of the same table are for another system (with a positron).

results.system_description: BeO at R = 2.115 bohr, all electrons, the singlet calculation of the paper (6 up, 6 down), clamped nuclei
results.variant: FermiNet (Spencer et al. architecture), bare molecule
results.source_location: Supplementary Data Tables, Beryllium oxide, singlet, bond length 2.115 a0, 'Bare' column
results.eligibility_evidence: VMC energy of the bare molecule with the Spencer et al. FermiNet; 'Errors in energy expectation values are evaluated using a reblocking approach' (main text), printed in the sigma column.
results.notes: Singlet BeO. Printed as '-89.845004' with sigma_Bare = 0.000024 in a separate column. N_up = N_down = 6. The instance is the sector N_up = N_down = 6: where the triplet lies lower (at 3.515 bohr the triplet row of the same table is below the singlet one), its lowest state is the M_S = 0 component of the triplet, to which the singlet energy is an upper bound. The positronic energies of the same table are for another system.
